Fuji" (also titled Boy and Mt. Fuji". Hokusai lived from 1760-1849. This work shows a boy in a tree, over river rapids, with a basket suspended below him. He is playing a flute, while looking at Mt. Fuji, one of the most famous symbols of Japan. This picture of a child's life looks simple on the surface but has a deeper resonance and meaning, painted late in the artist's life. The basket shows the boy is supposed to be fishing for food/market produce; it is a fishing creel and this is a good fishing spot over the river rocks. However, the boy has chosen to play flute and view nature instead. He is suspended with careful but relaxed balance in the tree between heaven and earth. This shows, in one interpretation, the balance that one has in work and life and choosing to pursue artistic and philosophical, momentary pursuits rather than a focus on labor and prosperity.
